page: Vultr voc-c-2c-4gb-50s-amd is an entry-level virtual machine belonging to the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to a single physical AMD EPYC core with 2 threads per core, utilizing a shared CPU allocation model. The system operates on the x86_64 architecture at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz, supported by 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per core, and includes 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark results show a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance under stress-ng is in the top tier, and single-threaded operations like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression rank in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance falls into the average category. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is average, but small-block read-only bandwidth is weak, placing in the bottom 25%. Passmark CPU metrics, database operations, and Redis SET operations also rank in the bottom 25%, while static web serving throughput is poor, falling into the bottom 10%.

The shared CPU allocation introduces potential resource contention, which explains the lower multi-core and database benchmark scores despite strong single-core performance. This configuration offers a cost-effective entry point for workloads that require bursty single-threaded processing rather than sustained multi-core execution. It is suitable for lightweight applications, basic development environments, single-threaded utility scripts, and low-traffic web serving where high memory density and dedicated CPU resources are not required.
